You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words (not including the sentence given).
first: With their valuable skills and experience, elderly people can continue to make significant contributions to society.
body: With their valuable skills and experience, elderly people can continue to make significant contributions to society. Retirement does not have to mean the end of a useful life; instead, it can open a new chapter in which older people share what they have learned over decades. Many of them are still energetic and eager to stay involved.

In my own neighborhood, I have seen this again and again. A retired engineer repairs household appliances for free every weekend, and a former teacher runs an after-school reading club for children whose parents work late. My grandfather, a retired doctor, is a particularly good example. Once a month he gives free health talks at our community center, and thanks to his advice, many neighbors now check their blood pressure regularly. These contributions may seem small, but they make the neighborhood a warmer, friendlier place. Moreover, by staying active, these elderly people keep themselves healthy and find their lives meaningful.

Society should therefore create more opportunities for older people to contribute, such as flexible part-time jobs and volunteer programs suited to their abilities. Young people, for their part, should respect the elderly, listen to their stories and learn from their experience. When the wisdom of age is valued, everyone benefits.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words (not including the sentence given).
first: Nowadays parents are increasingly aware that allowing kids more freedom to explore and learn on their own helps foster their independence and boost their confidence.
body: Nowadays parents are increasingly aware that allowing kids more freedom to explore and learn on their own helps foster their independence and boost their confidence. In the past, many parents tended to arrange everything for their children, from what to study to how to spend their weekends, leaving them little room to make their own choices.

Giving children freedom brings clear benefits. When kids are allowed to solve problems by themselves, they learn to think independently and take responsibility for their decisions. Even their mistakes become valuable lessons, teaching them what works and what does not. In addition, every small success they achieve on their own, such as building a model or cooking a simple meal, makes them believe in their abilities. I still remember how proud I felt when my parents first let me take the subway to school alone at the age of ten. That experience made me feel trusted and capable.

Of course, freedom does not mean a lack of guidance. Parents should set clear safety rules, offer advice when needed and be ready to step in when their children run into real difficulties. Within these limits, parents can let children plan a weekend outing or manage a small weekly allowance. With a proper balance between freedom and support, children can grow into independent and confident adults.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words (not including the sentence given).
first: As is known to all, gaining a sound knowledge of the basics is of vital importance for students to master an academic subject.
body: As is known to all, gaining a sound knowledge of the basics is of vital importance for students to master an academic subject. Just as a tall building cannot stand without a solid foundation, advanced study is impossible without a firm grasp of the fundamentals. Whether it is mathematics, physics or a foreign language, every subject is built on a set of basic concepts and skills.

The basics matter for two reasons. First, they are the building blocks of more complex knowledge. A student who has not mastered basic English grammar and vocabulary, for example, will find it almost impossible to read academic papers in English. Second, a solid foundation makes further learning easier and faster. Students who truly understand the basic concepts of mathematics can apply them flexibly to new problems, whereas those who merely memorize formulas often get lost when a question is slightly changed.

Unfortunately, some students, impatient for quick results, skip the basics to tackle difficult problems. To avoid this, they should be patient, review the fundamentals regularly and make sure that they understand them rather than merely memorize them. Teachers can also help by emphasizing core concepts in class and checking that students have mastered them before moving on. With strong fundamentals, students can go much further in their academic pursuits.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
first: Today there is a growing awareness that mental well-being needs to be given as much attention as physical health.
body: Today there is a growing awareness that mental well-being needs to be given as much attention as physical health. Faced with heavy academic pressure, fierce competition and a fast pace of life, more and more people suffer from anxiety, stress or low mood.

Mental well-being deserves such attention because it affects every part of our lives. Many students, for example, are physically fit but so anxious before exams that they can hardly focus in class or enjoy time with friends. In fact, the mind and the body are closely linked: long-term stress may cause sleep problems and weaken the immune system. Yet unlike a fever or a broken arm, mental health problems are often invisible and easy to ignore, and some people even feel ashamed to seek help.

Therefore, we should care for our minds as carefully as we care for our bodies. Individuals can keep a regular routine, exercise often and talk with friends when they feel down. If the problem persists, they should seek professional help. Colleges should provide easily accessible counseling services and help remove the stigma surrounding mental health. After all, a truly healthy life requires both a sound body and a sound mind.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
first: When faced with differing opinions, we should try to reach agreement through friendly discussion and reasonable argument.
body: When faced with differing opinions, we should try to reach agreement through friendly discussion and reasonable argument. Whether in a dormitory, a classroom or a workplace, disagreements are unavoidable, and how we handle them often determines whether a problem is solved or made worse.

Friendly discussion creates an atmosphere of mutual respect. When people feel that their views are heard, they are more willing to listen to others instead of getting defensive. Reasonable argument, in addition, ensures that decisions are based on facts and logic rather than emotion or stubbornness. Last term, my roommates and I disagreed about when to turn off the lights at night. Instead of quarreling, we each explained our needs calmly and finally agreed on a schedule that worked for everyone. The discussion not only solved the problem but also strengthened our friendship.

To reach agreement in this way, we should keep an open mind, express our views politely and support them with evidence. We should also be willing to admit that others may be right and that we may be wrong. Ultimately, the goal of a discussion is not to win but to find the best solution together.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
first: It is widely accepted that an important goal of education is to help students learn how to learn.
body: It is widely accepted that an important goal of education is to help students learn how to learn. In a world where knowledge keeps growing and changing, no school can teach students everything they will need in the future.

Learning how to learn means mastering the skills that make lifelong learning possible: setting goals, finding and evaluating information, managing time and reflecting on one’s own progress. Students who have these skills can teach themselves new subjects long after they leave school. By contrast, those who are used to memorizing whatever their teachers tell them may feel helpless when facing unfamiliar problems. As the saying goes, “Give a man a fish and you feed him for a day; teach him to fish and you feed him for a lifetime.”

To achieve this goal, teachers should shift from simply delivering knowledge to guiding students as they explore it, for example through projects, discussions and research tasks. Schools can also teach study skills directly, such as how to take notes and review effectively. Students, in turn, should take an active role in their own learning. Once they know how to learn, they will never stop growing.
